subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept the bounded longer isolated-cron setup window proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 as the canonical fix for this issue?
rationale: The fix is narrow and proof-positive, but it intentionally changes availability behavior by letting stuck setup hold cron capacity longer than the current 60s ceiling.

options.title: Accept bounded watchdog
options.body: Land the derived setup-timeout budget from the open PR and treat separate Codex/backend stalls as follow-up issues.

options.title: Require stricter cap
options.body: Ask for a lower maximum or additional runtime proof before merging the watchdog change.

options.title: Prefer configurability
options.body: Pause the open PR and require an explicit operator-tunable cron watchdog surface instead.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the derived setup-timeout budget from the open PR and treat separate Codex/backend stalls as follow-up issues.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-main and release-area signal for cron watchdog behavior, while the open PR author owns the proposed implementation details.
